phase3_findings.description: No test checks that a History switch drops appended blocks (line 392 `if (!options.restore) appendedRef.current = [];`, also line 375 in the no-getConversation branch), though README line 75 and the appendBlocks TSDoc promise it; the only History test (ChatWidget.test.tsx 239-251) never calls appendBlocks.

An appendBlocks call after unmount() queues the call and schedules flush, which finds no handle and reschedules itself every 10 ms forever; the call is dropped with no log. Pre-existing replay mechanism shared by every handle method, newly reachable through host-driven appendBlocks.
appendBlocks silently drops malformed entries (null or no string type) from an array that also holds valid ones; the warning fires only when nothing renders.

The PR bundles changes unrelated to appendBlocks against CONTRIBUTING.md line 20 (one concern per PR), none named in the PR description: viewport re-clamping (ChatWidget.tsx 228-257), CSS size caps (570-578), the react-chatbot-kit CommonJS interop unwrap (26, 52-56) and two viewport tests (ChatWidget.test.tsx 61-111).
No test covers the guard that forgets the saved conversation ID only while storage still holds the one that failed (pending restore followed by a History switch).
No test pins down that { blocks: [], sources: [...] } still renders its sources; dropping messages.length === 0 from the silent condition would pass every test.
After a failed turn the composer gets the text back but not the attachments, so a retry from the refilled text silently sends without the files (README promises only the text).
A turn with blocks: [] and sources that all lack a title renders nothing and ends silently with no reply, apology or log, while the docs describe the silent case as an empty array with no sources.

The silent-turn comment (ChatController.ts 389-390) and SendMessageResponse.blocks TSDoc (types.ts 110-114) name only the no-sources case, while non-empty sources that render nothing also end the turn silently.
README line 75 says appended blocks stay when the saved conversation is restored without saying they live only in widget memory and are gone after a page reload.
The ChatWidgetHandle.appendBlocks TSDoc does not say appended blocks exist only in the widget and are lost on reload.

The kit-import comment's claim that under Vite the default import is the whole module.exports is probably wrong (Vite's interop returns .default when __esModule is set); unconfirmed from the repository.
The line 416 comment describes only the failed-load case, while ok is also false when the restore was abandoned by a reset.
